metadata.title: Entropy Compression Method and Legitimate Colorings in Projective Planes

nodes.name: Bad setting
nodes.statement: A bad setting is a pair $(Z, c)$ where $Z \subset V$ is a subset of vertices of a graph $G$ and $c$ is a given coloring of $Z$.
nodes.statement_clean: A bad setting is a pair consisting of a vertex subset and a coloring of it that is to be avoided.

nodes.name: Bad setting indexing data $(\mathcal{Z}, C_i, k_i, m_i, l_i, E, d_l)$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{Z} := \{ Z \subset V : \exists\, c \text{ s.t.\ } (Z,c) \text{ is a bad setting}\}$ indexed by $I \subset \mathbb{N}$. For each $i \in I$: $C_i := \{ c : (Z_i,c) \text{ bad}\}$; $k_i$ fixed vertices give at most $m_i$ extensions; $l_i := |Z_i| - k_i$; $E := \{ l_i : i \in I\}$; $Q_l(v)$ the subsets containing $v$ with $l_j = l$, and $d_l := \max_{v \in V} |Q_l(v)|$.
nodes.statement_clean: Combinatorial data attached to a bad-setting family used to bound the colorings in the entropy compression argument.

nodes.name: Variable version of the Lov\'asz Local Lemma setting
nodes.statement: $\Psi = \{\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_n\}$ a set of independent discrete random variables on a finite set, $\mathcal{A} = \{A_x : x \in X\}$ a family of bad events determined by them, and $c(A_x)$ the configurations of $\mathrm{vbl}(A_x)$ that make $A_x$ occur.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard variable-version LLL setup: independent finite-valued variables and bad events depending on subsets of them.

nodes.name: Register vector $R$ for the entropy compression algorithm
nodes.statement: At step $i$, if a bad setting $(\mathrm{vbl}(A_y),c)$ is created, set $R_i = (\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ with $\alpha := l_y$, $\beta \in [d_{l_y}]$ the position of $\mathrm{vbl}(A_y)$ in the indexed family, and $\gamma \in [m_y]$ the label of the values of the $l_y$ variables; otherwise $R_i$ is empty.
nodes.statement_clean: The history register that stores, at each step, the size, position and value-label of the bad event triggered.

nodes.name: Projective plane $P_n = (P,L)$ of order $n$
nodes.statement: A finite projective plane of order $n$ is a pair $P_n = (P,L)$ with $|P| = |L| = n^2 + n + 1$, every line containing $n+1$ points, and every point lying on $n+1$ lines.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard finite projective plane combinatorial structure.

nodes.name: Type of a line; legitimate coloring; bad pair
nodes.statement: For a $\mathsf{d}$-coloring $f : P \to \{1,\ldots,\mathsf{d}\}$ the type of a line $\ell$ is $t_{\ell,f} := (|\ell \cap f^{-1}(1)|,\ldots,|\ell \cap f^{-1}(\mathsf{d})|)$. The coloring is legitimate if all lines have distinct types; a pair $\{\ell_i,\ell_j\}$ with $t_{\ell_i,f}=t_{\ell_j,f}$ is a bad pair.
nodes.statement_clean: A legitimate coloring is one whose induced line-types are all distinct; equal-type pairs are bad.

nodes.name: Dangerous pair
nodes.statement: Let $f \colon P \setminus S \to \{1,\ldots,\mathsf{d}\}$ be a partial $\mathsf{d}$-coloring of $P_n$. A pair $\{\ell_i,\ell_j\}$ with $\ell_i \neq \ell_j$ is dangerous if $d_1(t_{\ell_i,f}, t_{\ell_j,f}) \leq 22 \ln n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two distinct lines form a dangerous pair when their type vectors differ by at most $22\ln n$ in $\ell_1$ distance.

nodes.name: Optimal block size $\underline{m}$
nodes.statement: $\underline{m} := \arg\min_m \frac{m}{m-1}(m!\,a\cdot b\,(m-1))^{1/m}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Block size minimizing the entropy-compression bound for projective-plane colorings.

nodes.name: Lemma 1: $X_i$ determined by the register
nodes.statement: At each step $i$, the set $X_i$ of uncolored variables after step $i$ is uniquely determined by the vector $(R_j)_{j\leq i}$.
assumptions: The entropy compression algorithm of Section 2.1 is executed
$R_j$ is the register entry recorded at step $j$
conclusions: $X_i$ is a function of $(R_j)_{j \leq i}$ alone

nodes.name: Lemma 2: Reconstruction of colors from $((R_j)_{j\leq i},\phi_i)$
nodes.statement: $((R_j)_{j\leq i},\phi_i)$ stores sufficient information to deduce which colors were used at each step of the algorithm until step $i$.
assumptions: The entropy compression algorithm is executed
$\phi_i$ is the configuration of the variables at step $i$
$R_j$ is the register entry at step $j$
conclusions: The colors used at every step $\leq i$ can be reconstructed from $((R_j)_{j\leq i},\phi_i)$

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (variant of Esperet--Parreau)
nodes.statement: There exists a coloring of $V$ that avoids all bad settings using $\lceil \gamma \sup_{i \in I} (d_{l_i} m_i)^{1/l_i} \rceil$ colors, with $\phi_E(x) := 1 + \sum_{i\in E} x^i$, $\gamma := \phi_E'(\tau)$ and $\phi_E(\tau) - \tau \phi_E'(\tau) = 0$.
assumptions: $G$ is a graph with vertex set $V$
Bad settings are described by the data $(\mathcal{Z}, C_i, k_i, m_i, l_i, E, d_l)$ of Definition DP418.2
$\phi_E(x) := 1 + \sum_{i\in E} x^i$ and $\tau$ satisfies $\phi_E(\tau) - \tau\phi_E'(\tau) = 0$
conclusions: There exists a vertex-coloring of $V$ avoiding all bad settings using $\lceil \gamma \sup_{i \in I} (d_{l_i} m_i)^{1/l_i} \rceil$ colors

nodes.name: Fact 1: Existence of a small set $S$ hitting every line
nodes.statement: Let $P_n = (P,L)$ be a projective plane of order $n$. Then there exists $S \subset P$ such that for all $\ell \in L$, $\tfrac{1}{2}\ln n \leq |\ell \cap S| \leq 11 \ln n$.
assumptions: $P_n = (P,L)$ is a projective plane of order $n$
conclusions: There exists $S \subset P$ such that $\tfrac{1}{2}\ln n \leq |\ell \cap S| \leq 11\ln n$ for every line $\ell \in L$

nodes.name: Corollary on $|S|$
nodes.statement: The cardinality of $S$ satisfies $|S| \leq \frac{(n^2+n+1)\, 11 \ln n}{n+1}$.
assumptions: $P_n = (P,L)$ is a projective plane of order $n$
$S \subset P$ is the set guaranteed by Fact 1

nodes.name: Fact 2: Existence of a partial coloring with bounded dangerous incidences
nodes.statement: For $\mathsf{d} \geq 8$, $a \geq 1$ and $b \geq 4$, and $n$ large enough, there exists a partial coloring $f \colon P \setminus S \to \{1,\ldots,\mathsf{d}\}$ such that (1) no point in $S$ belongs to more than $b$ lines involved in dangerous pairs and (2) no line in $L$ forms a dangerous pair with more than $a$ other lines.
assumptions: $\mathsf{d} \geq 8$, $a \geq 1$, $b \geq 4$
$P_n$ is a projective plane of order $n$ with $n$ sufficiently large
$S$ is the set from Fact 1
conclusions: There exists a partial $\mathsf{d}$-coloring $f \colon P\setminus S \to \{1,\ldots,\mathsf{d}\}$
No point in $S$ belongs to more than $b$ lines involved in dangerous pairs
No line of $L$ forms a dangerous pair with more than $a$ other lines

nodes.name: Proposition: Legitimate coloring of $P_n$ via entropy compression
nodes.statement: There exists a legitimate coloring of $P_n$ using $\max\bigl(\mathsf{d}(n,a,b),\, \lceil \min_m \tfrac{m}{m-1}(m!\,a\cdot b\,(m-1))^{1/m} \rceil\bigr)$ colors, where $\mathsf{d}(n,a,b)$ is the number of colors needed to guarantee a partial coloring $f \colon P \setminus S \to [\mathsf{d}(n,a,b)]$ in which no point belongs to more than $a\cdot b$ dangerous pairs.
assumptions: $P_n$ is a projective plane of order $n$
Facts 1 and 2 hold for parameters $a, b, \mathsf{d}$
$\mathsf{d}(n,a,b)$ is large enough that the partial coloring of Fact 2 exists
conclusions: There exists a legitimate coloring of $P_n$ using $\max(\mathsf{d}(n,a,b), \lceil \min_m \tfrac{m}{m-1}(m!\,a\cdot b\,(m-1))^{1/m}\rceil)$ colors

nodes.name: Esperet--Parreau theorem (entropy compression)
nodes.statement: The entropy compression method gives a coloring avoiding forbidden configurations whenever, for each configuration $(H,c)$ and vertex $v$ of $H$, $k_{(H,c)}$ fixed other vertices determine the extension up to congruence.
assumptions: The problem can be stated as forbidding configurations on a graph $G$
For any $(H,c)$ and vertex $v$ of $H$ there are $k_{(H,c)}$ fixed vertices that uniquely determine the extension
conclusions: A coloring avoiding the forbidden configurations exists, with explicit color-count bound

nodes.name: Alon--Füredi bound for legitimate $8$-colorings
nodes.statement: If the order of $P_n$ is greater than $10^{250}$, then $5 \leq \chi(P_n) \leq 8$.
assumptions: $P_n$ is a projective plane of order $n > 10^{250}$

nodes.name: McDiarmid bounded-differences inequality (Corollary 2.8 of \v{S}ileikis)
nodes.statement: An improved Hoeffding--Azuma-type concentration inequality for sums of dependent random variables under bounded-difference conditions.
assumptions: Random variables satisfy bounded-difference conditions
conclusions: Sharp upper-tail bound used to obtain the $11 \ln n$ upper bound in Fact 1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2 (induction on $i$)
nodes.statement: By induction on $i$. The base case $i = 1$ is direct; the inductive step splits on whether $R_i$ is empty or $R_i = (\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary on $|S|$
nodes.statement: Counting incidences: every point of $S$ lies on $n+1$ lines and $|L| = n^2+n+1$, so $\max_{\ell} |\ell \cap S| \geq \tfrac{|S|(n+1)}{n^2+n+1}$; combine with Fact 1's upper bound $|\ell\cap S|\leq 11\ln n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 1
nodes.statement: The argument of Alon--F\"uredi (which gives the upper bound $20 \ln n$ for large $n$) is sharpened by applying Corollary 2.8 of \v{S}ileikis (an improvement of Hoeffding--Azuma due to McDiarmid) to lower the bound to $11\ln n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Fact 2
nodes.statement: Same probabilistic argument as in Lemma 2.6, Lemma 2.7 and Proposition 2.8 of Alon--F\"uredi, with $a$ and $b$ allowed to take values larger than the original $a=1, b=4$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition (legitimate coloring of $P_n$)
nodes.statement: Fix a partial coloring with $\mathsf{d}(n,a,b)$ colors guaranteed by Fact 2; then with $E = \{\underline{m}\}$ and $\phi_E(x) = 1 + x^{\underline{m}}$, solve $\phi_E(\tau) - \tau\phi_E'(\tau) = 0$ to get $\tau = (\underline{m}-1)^{-1/\underline{m}}$ and apply Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Modified Moser--Tardos / Esperet--Parreau entropy compression algorithm
nodes.statement: Iteratively assigns sampled values to the smallest-index uncolored variable; when a bad setting is created, uncolors the involved variables and records $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ in the register $R$.
input: Fixed orderings on $\{\mathrm{vbl}(A_x) : \psi_j \in \mathrm{vbl}(A_x), l_x = l\}$ and on the $m_x$ ways to sample $l_x$ variables generating each bad setting
output: Register $R$ recording the trace of bad settings
Final configuration $\phi_t$ of the variables (a coloring avoiding all bad settings if the algorithm halts)

nodes.name: Legitimate coloring problem for projective planes
nodes.statement: Find the minimum number of colors $\chi(P_n)$ such that there exists a legitimate $\chi(P_n)$-coloring of the projective plane $P_n$.

nodes.name: Variable-version forbidden-configuration coloring
nodes.statement: Given a graph $G = (V,E)$ and a family of bad settings $(Z,c)$ on $V$, find a vertex-coloring of $V$ avoiding all bad settings.

nodes.name: Alon--Füredi conjecture: $6 \leq \chi(P_n) \leq 7$
nodes.statement: Alon and F\"uredi conjectured that $6 \leq \chi(P_n) \leq 7$ for large values of $n$; this is still open.

nodes.name: Gap between small and large orders
nodes.statement: It remains open whether the gap between small and large orders of $P_n$ shown in Figure 1 is intrinsic to the legitimate-coloring problem or an artifact of the entropy-compression method.

nodes.name: Remark 1: lossless compression and the new register entry $\gamma$
nodes.statement: The variant adds the label $\gamma$ of the partial configuration to the register $R$; this preserves lossless compression (Lemma 2) and removes the second Esperet--Parreau constraint involving $k_{(H,c)}$.

nodes.name: Remark 2: uniform-case limitation
nodes.statement: Because $d_l$ and $m_i$ weight every bad setting equally, the analysis only handles the uniform case; non-uniform weighting (as in Achlioptas--Iliopoulos--Sinclair) is needed for sharper $k$-SAT bounds.

nodes.name: Remark 2 (Section 3): optimization formulation for large $n$
nodes.statement: For large $n$, the proposition reduces to: minimize $g(a,b,m,n) = n$ subject to $\frac{m}{m-1}(m!\,a\cdot b\,(m-1))^{1/m} \leq \mathsf{d}$ and $1 - (P_a + P_b) > 0$.

nodes.name: Constant $K$ in the dangerous-pair probability bounds
nodes.statement: $K := 2^\mathsf{d} \binom{22 \log n + \mathsf{d}}{\mathsf{d}} \dfrac{\mathsf{d}^{\mathsf{d}/2}}{[2\pi(n + 1 - 11\log n - n^{1/2})]^{(\mathsf{d}-1)/2}}$.

nodes.name: Base case: $\phi_1$ from $(\Psi_1)_1$
nodes.statement: After the first step, $\phi_1$ has only the first variable colored, with value $(\Psi_1)_1$, so the lemma holds trivially for $i=1$.

nodes.name: Inductive setup: identify $x_{\psi_j}$ via Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Assume the lemma for $i - 1$. By Lemma 1 we know $X_{i-1}$, hence we know $j = \min\{s : x_{\psi_s} \in X_{i-1}\}$, the variable colored at step $i$.

nodes.name: Case 1: $R_i$ empty
nodes.statement: If $R_i$ is empty, no bad setting was created and $\phi_{i-1}$ is obtained from $\phi_i$ by setting $x_{\psi_j}$ to $\circ$. By induction we know all earlier colors; the color at step $i$ is the value $\phi_i(x_{\psi_j})$.

nodes.name: Case 2: $R_i = (\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$
nodes.statement: If $R_i = (\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$, this identifies the bad setting $(\mathrm{vbl}(A_y),c)$ created at step $i$ and the values of its $l_y$ variables. Reverse-engineer $\phi_{i-1}$ by reassigning these values; the color at step $i$ is read off from $\gamma$.

nodes.name: Set up partial coloring via Fact 2
nodes.statement: Fix a partial coloring $f$ of $P_n$ using $\mathsf{d}(n,a,b)$ colors so that no point belongs to more than $a\cdot b$ dangerous pairs.

nodes.name: Compute $\tau$ and $\phi_E'(\tau)$
nodes.statement: With $E = \{\underline{m}\}$ and $\phi_E(x) = 1 + x^{\underline{m}}$, the equation $\phi_E(\tau) - \tau \phi_E'(\tau) = 0$ gives $\tau = (\underline{m}-1)^{-1/\underline{m}}$ and $\phi_E'(\tau) = \underline{m}(\underline{m}-1)^{(1-\underline{m})/\underline{m}}$.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 1 to extend $f$
nodes.statement: Substituting into the bound of Theorem 1 yields $\lceil \min_m \tfrac{m}{m-1}(m!\,a\cdot b\,(m-1))^{1/m} \rceil$ colors suffice to extend $f$ to a coloring with no bad pairs.

nodes.name: Incidence lower bound
nodes.statement: Since each point of $S$ lies on $n+1$ lines and $|L| = n^2 + n + 1$, $\max_{\ell\in L}|\ell\cap S| \geq \frac{|S|(n+1)}{n^2+n+1}$.

nodes.name: Combine with Fact 1 upper bound
nodes.statement: Using $|\ell \cap S| \leq 11\ln n$ from Fact 1, rearrangement gives $|S| \leq \frac{(n^2+n+1)\,11\ln n}{n+1}$.

nodes.name: Initialize variables to $\circ$
nodes.statement: Set $x_{\psi_1},\ldots,x_{\psi_n} \leftarrow \circ$; fix orderings on the indexed bad-event families and on the $m_x$ ways to generate each bad setting.

nodes.name: Main loop: assign value to smallest-index uncolored variable
nodes.statement: At step $i$, let $x_{\psi_j}$ be the uncolored variable of smallest index and assign to it the first unused entry of $\Psi_j$.

nodes.name: Halt / continue / repair branch
nodes.statement: If all variables are now non-$\circ$ and no bad setting exists, halt; if no bad setting was created but variables remain $\circ$, advance to the next step; if a bad setting $(\mathrm{vbl}(A_y),c)$ is created, fix the $k_y$ companions of $\psi_j$ in $\mathrm{vbl}(A_y)$ and reset the other $l_y$ variables to $\circ$.

nodes.name: Update register $R_i$
nodes.statement: If a bad setting was created, set $R_i := (\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ with $\alpha = l_y$, $\beta \in [d_{l_y}]$, $\gamma \in [m_y]$; otherwise leave $R_i$ empty.

nodes.name: Return $(R, \phi_t)$
nodes.statement: When the algorithm halts, return the register vector $R$ and the final configuration $\phi_t$ of the variables.
